extraction.name: ARC (AI2 Reasoning Challenge)
extraction.description: A dataset consisting of a question set of 7,787 natural grade-school science questions, partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set, along with the ARC Corpus of 14M science-related sentences and baseline models for advanced question answering.
extraction.creator: Peter Clark, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, Oyvind Tafjord
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The question set was assembled through several months of extensive search and investigation from a variety of sources of standardized test science questions. The ARC Corpus was mined from the Web using automatically constructed search queries from hand-written templates for science topics, collecting top documents, de-duplicating them, stripping text, and chunking into sentences.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Document analysis, Web Scraping, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Natural science questions authored for standardized tests from a variety of sources, plus web documents retrieved via search queries relevant to science and the AristoMini corpus.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For the ARC Corpus, collected web documents were de-duplicated, stripped down to text content, and chunked into sentences. The corpus was also augmented with the AristoMini corpus.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set based on whether two baseline solvers, an IR solver and a PMI solver, answered them incorrectly or not.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper notes that categorization of knowledge and reasoning types was based on a sample of 100 questions and involved subjective judgment, so category sizes are approximate.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper discusses retrieval bias in baseline methods toward sentences similar to the question and away from sentences that only partially match individually but together explain the answer, which affects performance on the Challenge set.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The Challenge Set definition only approximates the informal goal of hardness, and the corpus contains indirect mentions of relevant knowledge that are not trivial to exploit. The paper also notes scarcity of public real-world test data and that systems may need more advanced retrieval and reasoning methods.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended to encourage AI research in advanced question answering, provide a challenge to the community, support benchmarking with train/dev/test partitions, and optionally use the ARC Corpus for question answering systems.

name.evidence: The challenge presented here, called ARC (AI2 Reasoning Challenge), aims to address this limitation by posing questions that are hard to answer with simple baselines.

description.evidence: We present a new question set, text corpus, and baselines assembled to encourage AI research in advanced question answering.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: For ARC we have addressed this through several months of extensive search and investigation. The ARC Corpus was created by utilizing a major search engine to run a large series of search queries relevant to science.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: The ARC Dataset consists of a collection of 7787 natural science questions, namely questions authored for use on standardized tests. The ARC Corpus was created by utilizing a major search engine to run a large series of search queries relevant to science.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The ARC dataset consists of 7787 science questions, all non-diagram, multiple choice (typically 4-way multiple choice). They are drawn from a variety of sources. The top several documents from each search were collected and de-duplicated, and then the content of these documents was stripped down to capture just the text in each document. The corpus was then augmented with the AristoMini corpus

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: The top several documents from each search were collected and de-duplicated, and then the content of these documents was stripped down to capture just the text in each document. The resulting text was then chunked into sentences. The corpus was then augmented with the AristoMini corpus

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Operationally, we define a Challenge question as one that is answered incorrectly by both of two baseline solvers, described below.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: These sizes are necessarily approximate, as it requires a subjective judgement about the main challenge exhibited by different questions.

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: Questions vary in their target student grade level (as assigned by the examiners who authored the questions), ranging from 3rd grade to 9th

rai:dataBiases.evidence: However, the retrieval bias of the underlying IR methods is towards sentences that are all very similar to the question, and away from sentences that individually only partially match the question, but together fully explain the correct answer

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Although this only approximates the informal goal of it being a “hard” question, this definition nevertheless serves as a practical and useful filter. Although some of these mentions are indirect, and exploiting them is not trivial, it nevertheless provides a starting point for attacking the ARC Challenge.
